result:a1-proton-form-factors-high-preci.name: A1 high-precision determination of the electric and magnetic form factors of the proton

summary.plain: A1 measured about 1400 elastic electron-proton scattering cross sections at Mainz with errors below 0.2%, and extracted the proton's electric and magnetic form factors, which show features at the scale of the pion cloud and give the proton radius.

result:a1-proton-form-factors-high-preci.title: High-precision determination of the electric and magnetic form factors of the proton

result:a2-pi0-photoproduction-proton-mam.name: A2 measurement of pi0 photoproduction on the proton at MAMI C

summary.plain: A2 measured the differential cross sections of neutral-pion photoproduction on the proton up to a centre-of-mass energy of 1.9 GeV with unprecedented statistics and full angular coverage, increasing the world data on this reaction by about 47%.

result:a2-pi0-photoproduction-proton-mam.title: Measurement of pi0 photoproduction on the proton at MAMI C

result:a4-beam-transverse-asymmetry-wide.name: A4: beam transverse single-spin asymmetry from 315 MeV to 1.5 GeV

summary.plain: A4 measured how a transversely polarised electron beam scatters differently from protons at five beam energies, which probes the exchange of two photons between electron and proton. The data point to contributions from excited states of the proton that no current calculation reproduces.

result:a4-beam-transverse-asymmetry-wide.title: Study of Two-Photon Exchange via the Beam Transverse Single Spin Asymmetry in Electron-Proton Elastic Scattering at Forward Angles over a Wide Energy Range

result:a4-strange-form-factors-backward-.name: A4: backward-angle asymmetry and separated strange form factors at Q^2 = 0.22 (GeV/c)^2

The two together separate, for the first time at this point, the strange quarks' electric and magnetic contributions to the proton.

result:a4-strange-form-factors-backward-.title: Measurement of Strange Quark Contributions to the Vector Form Factors of the Proton at Q^2=0.22 (GeV/c)^2

result:a4-strange-form-factors-q2-0230-2.name: A4: strange-quark contribution to the proton's form factors at Q^2 = 0.230 (GeV/c)^2

result:a4-strange-form-factors-q2-0230-2.title: Measurement of Strange Quark Contributions to the Nucleon's Form Factors at Q^2=0.230 (GeV/c)^2

result:act-cmb-lensing-first-detection-2.name: Detection of the Power Spectrum of Cosmic Microwave Background Lensing by the Atacama Cosmology Telescope

result:adone-new-3-1-gev-particle-proper.name: Preliminary Result of Frascati (ADONE) on the Nature of a New 3.1-GeV Particle Produced in e+e- Annihilation

result:adone-new-3-1-gev-particle-proper.title: Preliminary Result of Frascati (ADONE) on the Nature of a New 3.1-GeV Particle Produced in e+e- Annihilation

result:aegis-pulsed-antihydrogen-2021.title: Pulsed production of antihydrogen

result:ags-two-neutrinos-observation-196.title: Observation of High-Energy Neutrino Reactions and the Existence of Two Kinds of Neutrinos

result:alice-hypertriton-lifetime-2019.name: (Anti-)hypertriton lifetime measurement in Pb-Pb collisions at 5.02 TeV

summary.plain: ALICE measured how long a rare, fragile nucleus called the hypertriton survives before decaying, using lead-lead collisions at the LHC. result:alice-jpsi-suppression-pbpb-2012.title: J/psi suppression at forward rapidity in Pb-Pb collisions at sqrt(s_NN) = 2.76 TeV

result:alice-strangeness-enhancement-pp-.name: First observation of strangeness enhancement in high-multiplicity pp collisions

result:alice-strangeness-enhancement-pp-.title: Enhanced production of multi-strange hadrons in high-multiplicity proton-proton collisions

result:alpha-fine-structure-2020.title: Investigation of the fine structure of antihydrogen

result:alpha-g-gravity-2023.key_value_text: Antihydrogen released from the trap behaves consistently with gravitational attraction; antigravity ruled out in this case
result:alpha-g-gravity-2023.name: Observation of the effect of gravity on the motion of antimatter

result:alpha-laser-cooling-2021.key_value_text: Median transverse energy reduced by more than an order of magnitude; 1S–2S line about four times narrower

result:alpha-laser-cooling-2021.significance: Median transverse energy reduced by more than an order of magnitude (no sigma level stated)

result:alpha-laser-cooling-2021.title: Laser cooling of antihydrogen atoms

result:alpha-resonant-transitions-2012.title: Resonant quantum transitions in trapped antihydrogen atoms

result:alpha-trapped-antihydrogen-2010.title: Trapped antihydrogen

result:amore-i-ca40-double-electron-capt.name: A study of neutrinoless double electron capture in $^{40}$Ca from the AMoRE experiment

summary.plain: Using the AMoRE-I calcium-molybdate crystals, AMoRE searched for neutrinoless double electron capture of calcium-40 and saw no significant excess, setting a half-life lower limit of 1.7 x 10^22 years at 90% confidence.

result:amore-i-ca40-double-electron-capt.title: A study of neutrinoless double electron capture in $^{40}$Ca from the AMoRE experiment

result:amore-i-improved-limit-2025.name: Improved limit on neutrinoless double beta decay of $^{100}$Mo from AMoRE-I

summary.plain: After over two years with 18 crystals, AMoRE-I saw no indication of neutrinoless double beta decay of molybdenum-100 and set a lower limit of 2.9 x 10^24 years on its half-life at 90% confidence.

result:amore-i-improved-limit-2025.title: Improved limit on neutrinoless double beta decay of $^{100}$Mo from AMoRE-I

result:amore-ii-lmo-calorimeters-2025.name: Development of MMC-based lithium molybdate cryogenic calorimeters for AMoRE-II

result:amore-ii-lmo-calorimeters-2025.title: Development of MMC-based lithium molybdate cryogenic calorimeters for AMoRE-II

result:amore-pilot-first-results-2019.name: First Results from the AMoRE-Pilot neutrinoless double beta decay experiment

summary.plain: In its first results AMoRE-Pilot found no evidence for neutrinoless double beta decay of molybdenum-100 and set a lower limit of 9.5 x 10^22 years on its half-life at 90% confidence.

result:amore-pilot-first-results-2019.title: First Results from the AMoRE-Pilot neutrinoless double beta decay experiment

result:amore-pilot-improved-limit-2024.name: Background study of the AMoRE-pilot experiment

result:amore-pilot-improved-limit-2024.title: Background study of the AMoRE-pilot experiment

result:ceres-rho-modification-pb-au-2006.name: CERES modification of the rho meson in central Pb-Au collisions

summary.plain: With the upgraded CERES detector, the electron-pair excess in central lead-gold collisions clearly favours a strong broadening of the rho meson in the medium rather than a shift of its mass.

result:ceres-rho-modification-pb-au-2006.title: Modification of the rho meson detected by low-mass electron-positron pairs in central Pb-Au collisions at 158 A GeV/c

result:chamberlain-segre-antiproton-obse.key_value_text: First evidence of the antiproton on 21 September 1955, from momentum and velocity
result:chamberlain-segre-antiproton-obse.name: Observation of Antiprotons

summary.plain: Chamberlain, Segrè, Wiegand and Ypsilantis reported negatively charged particles with the mass of a proton, made when the Bevatron beam hit a target. This was the antiproton, the first antiparticle of a heavy particle to be found.

result:chamberlain-segre-antiproton-obse.title: Observation of Antiprotons

result:charm-ii-electroweak-parameters-1.name: Precision measurement of electroweak parameters from the scattering of muon-neutrinos on electrons

summary.plain: CHARM II counted thousands of rare events in which a muon neutrino or antineutrino bumps an electron. From them it found the weak mixing angle to be 0.2324 with an error of 0.0083, a clean test of the electroweak theory.

result:charm-ii-electroweak-parameters-1.title: Precision measurement of electroweak parameters from the scattering of muon-neutrinos on electrons

result:charm-structure-functions-1983.key_value_text: Structure functions F2 and xF3 and the antiquark momentum distribution determined as functions of x and Q^2
result:charm-structure-functions-1983.name: Experimental study of the nucleon structure functions and of the gluon distribution from charged-current neutrino and antineutrino interactions

summary.plain: CHARM measured how quarks share a nucleon's momentum by studying neutrino and antineutrino collisions in its detector at CERN. It determined the structure functions F2 and xF3 and the antiquark content as functions of the collision variables x and Q squared.

result:charm-structure-functions-1983.title: Experimental study of the nucleon structure functions and of the gluon distribution from charged-current neutrino and antineutrino interactions

result:chooz-initial-results-1997.key_value_text: No oscillation at 90 % CL for delta m^2 > 0.9e-3 eV^2 (maximum mixing) and sin^2(2 theta) > 0.18 (large delta m^2)
result:chooz-initial-results-1997.name: Initial Results from the CHOOZ Long Baseline Reactor Neutrino Oscillation Experiment

summary.plain: First results from a kilometre-baseline reactor experiment: the antineutrino rate matched expectation, so there was no sign of electron-antineutrino disappearance. This excluded the atmospheric-neutrino mixing region for electron antineutrinos and showed the electron-flavour mixing angle was small.

result:chooz-initial-results-1997.title: Initial Results from the CHOOZ Long Baseline Reactor Neutrino Oscillation Experiment

result:chooz-limits-1999.key_value_text: sin^2(2 theta) = 0.10 for large delta m^2 and delta m^2 > 7e-4 eV^2 for maximum mixing (90 % CL, no oscillation)
result:chooz-limits-1999.name: Limits on Neutrino Oscillations from the CHOOZ Experiment

summary.plain: With the full data sample CHOOZ still saw no antineutrino disappearance. For large mass differences it limited the mixing strength sin^2(2 theta) to about 0.10, a bound on the angle now called theta-13 that stood for over a decade.

result:chooz-limits-1999.title: Limits on Neutrino Oscillations from the CHOOZ Experiment

result:chorus-final-numu-nutau-2007.key_value_text: sin^2(2 theta_mu_tau) < 4.4e-4 at 90 % CL for large delta m^2
result:chorus-final-numu-nutau-2007.name: Final results on nu_mu to nu_tau oscillation from the CHORUS experiment

summary.plain: The final CHORUS analysis of its 1994-97 data found no sign of muon neutrinos turning into tau neutrinos. For large mass differences the mixing is below about 0.0004 (90 % confidence), 1.5 times tighter than the earlier CHORUS limit.

result:chorus-final-numu-nutau-2007.title: Final results on nu_mu to nu_tau oscillation from the CHORUS experiment

result:christenson-cronin-fitch-turlay-k.name: Evidence for the 2π Decay of the K20 Meson

summary.plain: Christenson, Cronin, Fitch and Turlay found that the long-lived neutral kaon sometimes decays into two pions, something forbidden if matter and antimatter behaved exactly alike. It was the first sign that nature treats matter and antimatter differently.

result:christenson-cronin-fitch-turlay-k.title: Evidence for the 2π Decay of the K20 Meson

result:clas-dvcs-beam-spin-asymmetry-obs.name: CLAS observation of exclusive DVCS beam-spin asymmetry

summary.plain: CLAS measured how often electrons of opposite spin orientation scatter from protons while radiating a photon. A large, predicted angular modulation showed that deeply virtual Compton scattering, a probe of the proton's internal structure, could be studied at Jefferson Lab.

result:clas-dvcs-beam-spin-asymmetry-obs.title: Observation of exclusive DVCS in polarized electron beam asymmetry measurements

result:clas12-dvcs-beam-spin-asymmetry-e.name: CLAS12 first DVCS beam-spin asymmetry measurement

summary.plain: CLAS12's first deeply virtual Compton scattering measurement, using 10.2 and 10.6 GeV electrons on protons. It provides over 2000 new data points that extend far beyond earlier data and tighten constraints on the proton's three-dimensional structure.

result:clas12-dvcs-beam-spin-asymmetry-e.title: First CLAS12 measurement of DVCS beam-spin asymmetries in the extended valence region

result:class-90-ghz-reionization-optical.name: A Measurement of the Largest-Scale CMB E-mode Polarization with CLASS
result:class-90-ghz-reionization-optical.significance: Reionization detected at 99.4% significance in cross-correlation with Planck

summary.plain: CLASS measured the largest-scale E-mode polarization of the Big Bang afterglow from the ground and, with Planck, obtained a value for the optical depth that records when the first stars reionized the universe, a first for a ground-based experiment.

result:class-90-ghz-reionization-optical.title: A Measurement of the Largest-Scale CMB E-mode Polarization with CLASS

result:cleo-charmless-semileptonic-b-evi.name: Observation of B-meson semileptonic decays to noncharmed final states

summary.plain: CLEO reported the first evidence that B mesons can decay semileptonically with no charm quark in the final state. The paper's title says observation; the abstract says first evidence.

result:cleo-charmless-semileptonic-b-evi.title: Observation of B-meson semileptonic decays to noncharmed final states

result:cleo-upsilon-three-states-observa.key_value_text: Three narrow resonances in e⁺e⁻ → hadrons at total energies between 9.4 and 10.4 GeV
result:cleo-upsilon-three-states-observa.name: Observation of Three Upsilon States

summary.plain: In 1980 the CLEO experiment at Cornell's new CESR ring observed three narrow resonances in electron-positron collisions at total energies between 9.4 and 10.4 GeV. They were interpreted as the lowest Upsilon states of a bottom quark and its antiquark. The CUSB experiment reported the same states in a paper submitted back to back.

result:cleo-upsilon-three-states-observa.title: Observation of Three Upsilon States

result:cmd-2-pion-form-factor-measuremen.key_value_text: Pion form factor measured for 0.6 < √s < 1.0 GeV with 0.8% systematic uncertainty
result:cmd-2-pion-form-factor-measuremen.name: High-statistics measurement of the pion form factor in the rho-meson energy range with the CMD-2 detector

summary.plain: CMD-2 measured the pion form factor, which describes how electron-positron collisions make pion pairs, between 0.6 and 1.0 GeV with a 0.8% systematic uncertainty from a data sample five times larger than its previous measurement.

result:cmd-2-pion-form-factor-measuremen.title: High-statistics measurement of the pion form factor in the rho-meson energy range with the CMD-2 detector

result:cmd-3-pipi-cross-section-measurem.key_value_text: Systematic uncertainty of 0.7% in the dominant rho-resonance region (about 62 pb⁻¹ below 1 GeV)
result:cmd-3-pipi-cross-section-measurem.name: Measurement of the e+e-→π+π- cross section from threshold to 1.2 GeV with the CMD-3 detector

summary.plain: CMD-3 measured how often electron-positron collisions between 0.32 and 1.2 GeV produce a pair of pions, reaching a systematic uncertainty of 0.7% near the rho resonance. This cross section is a key input to predictions of the muon's anomalous magnetic moment.

result:cmd-3-pipi-cross-section-measurem.title: Measurement of the e+e-→π+π- cross section from threshold to 1.2 GeV with the CMD-3 detector

result:cms-higgs-boson-observation-2012.name: Observation of a new boson at a mass of 125 GeV

summary.plain: CMS reported an excess of events above background near 125 GeV that, in its words, signals the production of a new particle, at a joint CERN seminar on 4 July 2012. The paper gives a mass of 125.3 ± 0.4 (stat) ± 0.5 (syst) GeV and says the two-photon decay indicates a boson with spin different from one.

result:cms-higgs-boson-observation-2012.title: Observation of a new boson at a mass of 125 GeV with the CMS experiment at the LHC

result:cms-higgs-boson-portrait-2022.name: A portrait of the Higgs boson ten years after the discovery

summary.plain: Ten years after the discovery, CMS reported what it calls the most up-to-date combination of its results on the Higgs boson's properties (decays, spin-parity, mass and production), together with a limit on Higgs boson pair production. The collaboration says that, within the uncertainties, all these observations are compatible with the Standard Model.

result:cms-higgs-boson-portrait-2022.title: A portrait of the Higgs boson by the CMS experiment ten years after the discovery

result:cms-higgs-to-bb-observation-2018.name: Observation of Higgs boson decay to bottom quarks
result:cms-higgs-to-bb-observation-2018.significance: 5.6σ observed (5.5σ expected), combination with H → bb̄ searches in other production processes

summary.plain: CMS reports the observation of the Higgs boson decaying to bottom quarks, which the paper calls the most prevalent decay mode (predicted branching fraction about 58%). The main contribution comes from events where the Higgs boson is produced together with a W or Z boson.

result:cms-higgs-to-bb-observation-2018.title: Observation of Higgs boson decay to bottom quarks

result:cms-higgs-to-tau-tau-observation-.name: Observation of the Higgs boson decay to tau leptons
result:cms-higgs-to-tau-tau-observation-.significance: 5.9σ observed (5.9σ expected), 13 TeV data combined with 7 and 8 TeV data

summary.plain: CMS reports the first observation of Higgs boson decays to tau leptons by a single experiment, from 13 TeV data combined with earlier 7 and 8 TeV data (observed significance 5.9 standard deviations). Tau leptons are heavy relatives of the electron.

result:cms-higgs-to-tau-tau-observation-.title: Observation of the Higgs boson decay to a pair of tau leptons with the CMS detector

result:cms-high-mass-dilepton-search-202.name: Search for new high-mass dilepton resonances and nonresonant phenomena (2016–2018 data)

summary.plain: CMS searched its 2016–2018 13 TeV data (up to 140 fb⁻¹) for electron or muon pairs from a heavy new particle and saw no significant deviation from the Standard Model background. The abstract says the limits are the most stringent to date on the masses of various spin-1 particles, spin-2 gravitons (Randall–Sundrum model) and spin-1 dark-matter mediators.

result:cms-high-mass-dilepton-search-202.title: Search for resonant and nonresonant new phenomena in high-mass dilepton final states at sqrt(s) = 13 TeV

aliases: Observation of the rare decay Bs0 -> mu+ mu- (CMS and LHCb combined)
result:cms-lhcb-bs-to-mumu-observation-2.name: Observation of the rare decay B⁰ₛ → μ⁺μ⁻ (CMS and LHCb combined)

summary.plain: CMS and LHCb combined their 2011–2012 data to make the first observation of a B_s meson decaying into two muons, a decay the Standard Model predicts to be very rare: about four in every billion B_s mesons produced.

result:cms-lhcb-bs-to-mumu-observation-2.title: Observation of the rare $B^0_s\to\mu^+\mu^-$ decay from the combined analysis of CMS and LHCb data

result:cms-long-range-near-side-correlat.name: Observation of long-range near-side angular correlations in pp collisions ("the ridge")

summary.plain: CMS reported the first observation, in proton-proton or proton-antiproton collisions, of a long-range 'near-side' correlation: in high-multiplicity 7 TeV collisions, pairs of particles are emitted in nearly the same azimuthal direction while far apart in pseudorapidity (angle relative to the beam).

result:cms-long-range-near-side-correlat.title: Observation of Long-Range Near-Side Angular Correlations in Proton-Proton Collisions at the LHC

result:cms-top-quark-mass-measurement-20.name: Measurement of the top quark mass: 171.77 ± 0.37 GeV

summary.plain: CMS measured the mass of the top quark, which its paper calls the most massive fundamental particle, as 171.77 ± 0.37 GeV from 13 TeV collision data; the abstract says the approach significantly improves the precision over previous measurements.

result:cms-top-quark-mass-measurement-20.title: Measurement of the top quark mass using a profile likelihood approach with the lepton+jets final states in proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s) = 13 TeV

summary.plain: CMS observed Higgs bosons produced together with a top quark and an anti-top quark. The paper explains that on-shell top quarks are too heavy to appear in Higgs boson decays, so this production process is how the Higgs boson's coupling to the top quark can be constrained.

result:cms-w-boson-mass-measurement-2024.name: High-precision measurement of the W boson mass

summary.plain: CMS measured the mass of the W boson, which the collaboration calls the best-precision measurement of the W mass at the LHC, and found it in agreement with the Standard Model prediction. The paper notes that a measurement by the CDF collaboration at the Tevatron disagrees strongly with both the Standard Model expectation and the other measurements.

result:cms-w-boson-mass-measurement-2024.title: High-precision measurement of the W boson mass with the CMS experiment

result:cogent-annual-modulation-2011.name: Search for an Annual Modulation in a P-type Point Contact Germanium Dark Matter Detector

summary.plain: Fifteen months of CoGeNT data showed a yearly rise and fall in the low-energy event rate, of unknown origin, that fit light dark matter. The significance was about 2.8 sigma, too low to claim a signal.

result:cogent-annual-modulation-2011.title: Search for an Annual Modulation in a P-type Point Contact Germanium Dark Matter Detector

result:cogent-detector-and-backgrounds-2.name: CoGeNT: A Search for Low-Mass Dark Matter using p-type Point Contact Germanium Detectors

summary.plain: A detailed study of the CoGeNT detector and its backgrounds found that no known background explains the low-energy excess or the earlier rate variation.

result:cogent-detector-and-backgrounds-2.title: CoGeNT: A Search for Low-Mass Dark Matter using p-type Point Contact Germanium Detectors

result:cogent-low-mass-excess-2010.name: Results from a Search for Light-Mass Dark Matter with a P-type Point Contact Germanium Detector

summary.plain: CoGeNT's germanium crystal in the Soudan mine recorded more low-energy events than its known backgrounds explained. The authors listed possible causes, including light dark matter, without claiming a discovery.

result:cogent-low-mass-excess-2010.title: Results from a Search for Light-Mass Dark Matter with a P-type Point Contact Germanium Detector

result:cogent-maximum-likelihood-2014.name: Maximum Likelihood Signal Extraction Method Applied to 3.4 years of CoGeNT Data

summary.plain: A statistical re-analysis of 3.4 years of CoGeNT data found a best-fit dark matter signal close to earlier reports but at only 1.7 sigma, well below the level that counts as evidence.

result:cogent-maximum-likelihood-2014.title: Maximum Likelihood Signal Extraction Method Applied to 3.4 years of CoGeNT Data

result:cogent-three-years-modulation-201.name: Search for An Annual Modulation in Three Years of CoGeNT Dark Matter Detector Data

summary.plain: With 3.4 years of data, CoGeNT still saw the yearly rate change, but about 4 to 7 times larger than a standard dark matter halo predicts; the authors suggested a non-standard halo as one possible explanation.

result:cogent-three-years-modulation-201.title: Search for An Annual Modulation in Three Years of CoGeNT Dark Matter Detector Data

result:coherent-argon-measurement-2021.name: First Measurement of Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering on Argon
result:coherent-argon-measurement-2021.significance: more than 3σ (two independent analyses, against the background-only hypothesis)

summary.plain: COHERENT reports the first measurement of neutrinos scattering coherently off argon nuclei, using a 24-kilogram liquid-argon detector at Oak Ridge. The rate is consistent with the Standard Model; together with the earlier caesium-iodide result, the collaboration says it confirms the existence of the process.

result:coherent-argon-measurement-2021.title: First Measurement of Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering on Argon

result:coherent-csi-cross-section-2022.key_value_text: Weak mixing angle sin²θW = 0.220 (+0.028/−0.026) at Q² ~ (50 MeV)², alongside constraints on non-standard interactions and a test of lepton flavor universality using the neutrino beam's timing structure
result:coherent-csi-cross-section-2022.name: Measurement of the Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering Cross Section on CsI by COHERENT

summary.plain: COHERENT re-measured the rate of neutrinos scattering coherently off caesium-iodide nuclei with more than twice the data of the first observation and a better model of nuclear recoils in the crystal. The collaboration calls it the most precise measurement of the process yet, and extracts the weak mixing angle at a momentum transfer near 50 MeV.

result:coherent-csi-cross-section-2022.title: Measurement of the Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering Cross Section on CsI by COHERENT

result:coherent-germanium-evidence-2024.name: Evidence of Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering with COHERENT's Germanium Array

summary.plain: COHERENT reports the first detection of neutrinos scattering coherently off natural germanium, using an array of eight high-purity germanium detectors at Oak Ridge. The collaboration calls the result evidence: it rejects the no-scattering hypothesis at 3.9σ, and the signal rate agrees with the Standard Model within 2σ.

result:coherent-germanium-evidence-2024.title: Evidence of Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering with COHERENT's Germanium Array

result:coherent-observation-2017.name: Observation of Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering

summary.plain: COHERENT reports observing neutrinos scatter off entire atomic nuclei at once, a process the paper says had evaded experimental demonstration for forty-three years after its first theoretical description. The detector was a 14.6-kilogram caesium-iodide crystal at the Spallation Neutron Source in Oak Ridge.

result:coherent-observation-2017.title: Observation of Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering

result:compass-a1-1420-observation-2015.name: COMPASS observation of a new narrow axial-vector meson a1(1420)

summary.plain: In pion-proton diffractive scattering COMPASS saw a narrow new signal that is a previously unseen axial-vector meson, the a1(1420), with a mass of about 1.41 GeV. It decays only to a f0(980) and a pion, which hints at an exotic nature.

result:compass-a1-1420-observation-2015.title: Observation of a new narrow axial-vector meson a1(1420)

result:compass-gluon-polarisation-quasi-.name: COMPASS gluon polarisation from high-pT hadron pairs

summary.plain: COMPASS measured how much of the proton's spin could come from the polarisation of its gluons, using photon-gluon fusion events that produce pairs of high-momentum hadrons. The result, consistent with zero within large errors, argued against a large gluon-spin contribution.

result:compass-gluon-polarisation-quasi-.title: Gluon polarization in the nucleon from quasi-real photoproduction of high-pT hadron pairs

result:connie-2019-data-limits-2022.key_value_text: Observed limit 66 (75) times the Standard Model prediction in 50-180 eV (Sarkis/Chavarria quenching), 95% CL
result:connie-2019-data-limits-2022.name: Search for coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering at a nuclear reactor with CONNIE 2019 data

summary.plain: With a silicon CCD array operated 30 metres from a reactor core and a detection threshold of 50 electronvolts, CONNIE saw no excess when the reactor was on. It set upper limits on the rate of neutrino-nucleus scattering of about 66 times the Standard Model prediction at the lowest energies.

result:connie-2019-data-limits-2022.title: Search for coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering at a nuclear reactor with CONNIE 2019 data

result:connie-first-results-2019.key_value_text: 95% CL limit for new physics at an event rate of 40 times the one expected from the Standard Model
result:connie-first-results-2019.name: Exploring low-energy neutrino physics with the Coherent Neutrino Nucleus Interaction Experiment (CONNIE)

summary.plain: The first results from the upgraded CONNIE detector found no excess of events when the reactor was on, reaching the best sensitivity then achieved at reactors for nuclear recoils near one keV, and limiting new physics to about 40 times the Standard Model rate.

result:connie-first-results-2019.title: Exploring low-energy neutrino physics with the Coherent Neutrino Nucleus Interaction Experiment (CONNIE)

result:cosine-100-anais-112-combined-202.name: Combined Annual Modulation Dark Matter Search with COSINE-100 and ANAIS-112
result:cosine-100-anais-112-combined-202.significance: 4.68 sigma and 3.53 sigma respective exclusions of the DAMA/LIBRA signal (1-6 keV and 2-6 keV)

summary.plain: COSINE-100 (Korea) and ANAIS-112 (Spain) combined their six-year data sets, found values consistent with no modulation, and report exclusions of the DAMA/LIBRA signal of 4.68 and 3.53 standard deviations in the 1-6 and 2-6 keV regions.

result:cosine-100-anais-112-combined-202.title: Combined Annual Modulation Dark Matter Search with COSINE-100 and ANAIS-112

result:cosine-100-annual-modulation-1-7-.key_value_text: Using a $\chi$-squared minimization method we observe best fit values for modulation amplitude and phase of 0.0092$\pm$0.0067 cpd/kg/keV and 127.2$\pm$45 d, respectively.
result:cosine-100-annual-modulation-1-7-.name: Search for a Dark Matter-Induced Annual Modulation Signal in NaI(Tl) with the COSINE-100 Experiment

summary.plain: From 1.7 years of data (97.7 kg yr) COSINE-100 fitted a yearly modulation amplitude of 0.0092 +/- 0.0067 counts per day per kg per keV and a phase of 127.2 +/- 45 days; the experiment is designed as a model-independent test of DAMA/LIBRA's claim.

result:cosine-100-annual-modulation-1-7-.title: Search for a Dark Matter-Induced Annual Modulation Signal in NaI(Tl) with the COSINE-100 Experiment

result:cosine-100-annual-modulation-3-ye.name: Three-year annual modulation search with COSINE-100

summary.plain: With 2.82 years of data and a 1 keV threshold, COSINE-100 fitted yearly-modulation amplitudes of 0.0067 +/- 0.0042 (1-6 keV) and 0.0051 +/- 0.0047 (2-6 keV) counts per day per kg per keV, for a phase fixed at 152.5 days.

result:cosine-100-annual-modulation-3-ye.title: Three-year annual modulation search with COSINE-100

result:cosine-100-dama-constraints-2021.name: Strong constraints from COSINE-100 on the DAMA dark matter results using the same sodium iodide target

summary.plain: Using 1.7 years of data and better event selection, COSINE-100 found no signal and ruled out, for the standard halo model, several ways of explaining the DAMA signals with dark-matter scattering on the same sodium-iodide target.

result:cosine-100-dama-constraints-2021.title: Strong constraints from COSINE-100 on the DAMA dark matter results using the same sodium iodide target

result:cosine-100-first-results-2018.name: An experiment to search for dark matter interactions using sodium iodide detectors

summary.plain: In its first 59.5 days of data COSINE-100 saw no excess of events above the expected background. The authors say this confirms that the annual-modulation signal claimed by DAMA is in severe tension with other experiments, if dark matter scatters with spin-independent interactions and follows the standard halo model.

result:cosine-100-first-results-2018.title: An experiment to search for dark matter interactions using sodium iodide detectors

result:cosine-100-full-dataset-annual-mo.name: COSINE-100 Full Dataset Challenges the Annual Modulation Signal of DAMA/LIBRA
result:cosine-100-full-dataset-annual-mo.significance: challenging the DAMA/LIBRA result with a confidence level greater than 3 sigma

summary.plain: Using all 6.4 years of data, COSINE-100 found no evidence of a yearly modulation signal and says this challenges the DAMA/LIBRA result at a confidence level above three standard deviations.

result:cosine-100-full-dataset-annual-mo.title: COSINE-100 Full Dataset Challenges the Annual Modulation Signal of DAMA/LIBRA

result:cosine-100-wimp-limits-0-7-kev-20.name: Limits on WIMP dark matter with NaI(Tl) crystals in three years of COSINE-100 data

summary.plain: With three years of data and the threshold lowered to 0.7 keV, COSINE-100 reports WIMP limits and says its findings strongly disfavour the DAMA signal as coming from WIMP interactions, fully excluding the DAMA/LIBRA three-sigma allowed regions.

result:cosine-100-wimp-limits-0-7-kev-20.title: Limits on WIMP dark matter with NaI(Tl) crystals in three years of COSINE-100 data

result:cosine-100u-crystal-encapsulation.name: Development and Initial Performance of an Upgraded NaI(Tl) Crystal Encapsulation for COSINE-100U

summary.plain: In the first performance paper of the upgraded detector, all eight crystals gave more light than in COSINE-100 (15.8 to 27.7 photoelectrons per keV) and the surface-alpha backgrounds fell.

result:cosine-100u-crystal-encapsulation.title: Development and Initial Performance of an Upgraded NaI(Tl) Crystal Encapsulation for COSINE-100U

result:cosine-100u-upgrade-2025.name: Upgrading the COSINE-100 Experiment for Enhanced Sensitivity to Low-Mass Dark Matter Detection

summary.plain: The COSINE-100 detector was upgraded and moved to Yemilab as COSINE-100U, with its photomultipliers coupled directly to the eight crystals (99.1 kg in all) to collect more light and probe lighter dark matter.

result:cosine-100u-upgrade-2025.title: Upgrading the COSINE-100 Experiment for Enhanced Sensitivity to Low-Mass Dark Matter Detection

result:cosinus-deep-underground-prototyp.name: Deep-underground dark matter search with a COSINUS detector prototype

summary.plain: The first underground test of a COSINUS sodium iodide cryogenic detector, a 3.67 g crystal at Gran Sasso, showed much better separation of electron events from nuclear recoils and set a dark matter limit with only 11.6 gram-days of data.

result:cosinus-deep-underground-prototyp.title: Deep-underground dark matter search with a COSINUS detector prototype

result:cosinus-facility-dama-challenge-2.name: COSINUS -- a model-independent challenge of the DAMA/LIBRA dark matter claim with cryogenic NaI detectors operated in a new low-background facility

summary.plain: COSINUS describes its finished underground facility at Gran Sasso and its plan for a first run with eight crystals, intended to test DAMA/LIBRA's signal without relying on assumptions about dark matter.

result:cosinus-facility-dama-challenge-2.title: COSINUS -- a model-independent challenge of the DAMA/LIBRA dark matter claim with cryogenic NaI detectors operated in a new low-background facility

result:cosinus-first-cryogenic-nai-detec.name: Results from the first cryogenic NaI detector for the COSINUS project

summary.plain: The first sodium iodide crystal run as a cryogenic detector for COSINUS, reading heat and light at millikelvin temperatures at once and telling particle types apart event by event.

result:cosinus-first-cryogenic-nai-detec.title: Results from the first cryogenic NaI detector for the COSINUS project

result:cosinus-remotes-particle-discrimi.name: Particle discrimination in a NaI crystal using the COSINUS remote TES design

summary.plain: A 3.7 g sodium iodide crystal cooled to millikelvin temperatures, read out through COSINUS's remote sensor design, could tell electron events from nuclear recoils above 15 keV, in an above-ground test.

result:cosinus-remotes-particle-discrimi.title: Particle discrimination in a NaI crystal using the COSINUS remote TES design

result:cosme-solar-axion-coupling-limit-.name: Recent results from the canfranc dark matter search with germanium detectors

summary.plain: The COSME germanium crystal also searched for axions made in the Sun, finding none and setting an upper limit on how strongly axions couple to light.

result:cosme-solar-axion-coupling-limit-.title: Recent results from the canfranc dark matter search with germanium detectors

result:cosme-wimp-exclusion-2001.name: Particle Dark Matter and Solar Axion Searches with a small germanium detector at the Canfranc Underground Laboratory

result:cosme-wimp-exclusion-2001.title: Particle Dark Matter and Solar Axion Searches with a small germanium detector at the Canfranc Underground Laboratory

result:cygno-light-yield-enhancement-202.name: Enhancing the light yield of He:CF$_4$ based gaseous detector

result:d0-top-quark-observation-1995.name: Observation of the Top Quark

result:d0-top-quark-observation-1995.title: Observation of the Top Quark

result:dama-libra-phase1-final-2013.title: Final model independent result of DAMA/LIBRA-phase1

result:dama-libra-phase2-first-results-2.name: First model independent results from DAMA/LIBRA-phase2

result:dama-libra-phase2-first-results-2.title: First model independent results from DAMA/LIBRA-phase2

result:dama-nai-evidence-summary-2003.name: Results from DAMA/NaI and perspectives for DAMA/LIBRA

result:danss-sterile-neutrino-exclusion-.title: Search for sterile neutrinos at the DANSS experiment

result:dasi-first-cmb-polarization-detec.name: Detection of Polarization in the Cosmic Microwave Background using DASI

result:dasi-first-cmb-polarization-detec.title: Detection of Polarization in the Cosmic Microwave Background using DASI

result:dasi-first-season-power-spectrum-.name: DASI First Results: A Measurement of the Cosmic Microwave Background Angular Power Spectrum

result:dasi-first-season-power-spectrum-.title: DASI First Results: A Measurement of the Cosmic Microwave Background Angular Power Spectrum

result:daya-bay-observation-2012.name: Observation of electron-antineutrino disappearance at Daya Bay

result:daya-bay-observation-2012.title: Observation of electron-antineutrino disappearance at Daya Bay

result:dear-kaonic-hydrogen-shift-width-.title: Measurement of the Kaonic Hydrogen X-Ray Spectrum

result:delight-mmc-resolution-2023.title: Optimum filter-based analysis for the characterization of a high-resolution magnetic microcalorimeter towards the DELight experiment

result:dmtpc-directional-sensitivity-201.title: Measurement of the directional sensitivity of DMTPC detectors

result:dmtpc-head-tail-observation-2007.name: Observation of the 'head-tail' effect in nuclear recoils of low-energy neutrons

result:dmtpc-head-tail-observation-2007.title: Observation of the 'head-tail' effect in nuclear recoils of low-energy neutrons

result:drift-iid-spin-dependent-2010.name: Spin-Dependent Limits from the DRIFT-IId Directional Dark Matter Detector

result:drift-iid-spin-dependent-2010.title: Spin-Dependent Limits from the DRIFT-IId Directional Dark Matter Detector

result:dune-far-site-excavation-2024.name: Excavation of the DUNE far-site caverns completed at SURF

result:dune-protodune-sp-performance-202.title: First results on ProtoDUNE-SP liquid argon time projection chamber performance from a beam test at the CERN Neutrino Platform

result:frejus-nucleon-decay-charged-lept.title: Results from the Fréjus experiment on nucleon decay modes with charged leptons

result:g0-forward-angle-strange-quark-20.name: G0 forward angle: parity-violating asymmetries over 0.12 < Q^2 < 1.0 GeV^2

result:g0-forward-angle-strange-quark-20.title: Strange Quark Contributions to Parity-Violating Asymmetries in the Forward G0 Electron-Proton Scattering Experiment

result:gargamelle-neutral-currents-1973.key_value_text: One electron event and as many as 166 hadronic neutral-current candidates (102 neutrino and 64 antineutrino events) by March 1973
result:gargamelle-neutral-currents-1973.name: Observation of neutrino-like interactions without muon or electron in the Gargamelle neutrino experiment

summary.plain: In 1973 the Gargamelle collaboration reported neutrino collisions in which no muon or electron came out, only hadrons, and one event of a neutrino knocking an electron forward. CERN calls this the first direct evidence of the weak neutral current, which the theory unifying the electromagnetic and weak forces required.

result:gargamelle-neutral-currents-1973.title: Observation of neutrino-like interactions without muon or electron in the Gargamelle neutrino experiment

result:garwin-lederman-weinrich-parity-o.key_value_text: A parity-violating asymmetry of 50 standard deviations in the distribution of decay electrons relative to the muon spin
result:garwin-lederman-weinrich-parity-o.name: Observations of the Failure of Conservation of Parity and Charge Conjugation in Meson Decays: the Magnetic Moment of the Free Muon

summary.plain: Garwin, Lederman and Weinrich showed that when a pion decays to a muon and the muon decays to an electron, the electrons come out preferentially in one direction relative to the muon spin. Nature distinguishes left from right in these weak decays.

result:garwin-lederman-weinrich-parity-o.title: Observations of the Failure of Conservation of Parity and Charge Conjugation in Meson Decays: the Magnetic Moment of the Free Muon

result:gbar-antihydrogen-production-2023.key_value_text: Excess over background indicating antihydrogen production at 3-4 standard deviations
result:gbar-antihydrogen-production-2023.name: Production of antihydrogen atoms by 6 keV antiprotons through a positronium cloud

summary.plain: GBAR reported its first antihydrogen: antiprotons from CERN’s ELENA ring were sent through a cloud of positronium atoms. The excess over background indicates antihydrogen production at a significance of 3 to 4 standard deviations.

result:gbar-antihydrogen-production-2023.title: Production of antihydrogen atoms by 6 keV antiprotons through a positronium cloud

result:genius-tf-first-naked-ge-detector.name: First 10 kg of Naked Germanium Detectors in Liquid Nitrogen installed in the GENIUS-Test-Facility

summary.plain: In May 2003 the first four bare germanium crystals were lowered into liquid nitrogen deep under the Gran Sasso mountain, the first underground test of a way to cut radioactive background.

result:genius-tf-first-naked-ge-detector.title: First 10 kg of Naked Germanium Detectors in Liquid Nitrogen installed in the GENIUS-Test-Facility

result:genius-tf-ii-iii-long-term-stabil.name: Status of GENIUS-TF-II and TF-III: the long-term stability of naked detectors in liquid nitrogen

summary.plain: After three years the six bare germanium detectors in liquid nitrogen could not be kept stable, which cast doubt on a full-size version of the idea.

result:genius-tf-ii-iii-long-term-stabil.title: Status of GENIUS-TF-II and TF-III: the long-term stability of naked detectors in liquid nitrogen

result:genius-tf-radon-daughter-backgrou.name: The GENIUS-test-facility: first results on background from 222Rn daughters

summary.plain: The first background analysis of the GENIUS-TF test facility found radon-daughter background 200 times above the simulation, still low enough for its dark matter goal.

result:genius-tf-radon-daughter-backgrou.title: The GENIUS-test-facility: first results on background from 222Rn daughters

result:gluex-beam-asymmetry-pi0-eta-2017.name: GlueX beam asymmetry for pi0 and eta photoproduction

summary.plain: GlueX's first physics result: how the outgoing neutral pions and eta mesons are produced preferentially along or across the photon's polarisation direction. The eta measurements were the first at these energies and constrain how such mesons are produced.

result:gluex-beam-asymmetry-pi0-eta-2017.title: Measurement of the beam asymmetry Σ for π0 and η photoproduction on the proton at Eγ = 9 GeV

result:gluex-jpsi-near-threshold-photopr.key_value_text: exponential slope of dσ/dt of 1.67 ± 0.39 GeV^-2 at 10.7 GeV average energy
result:gluex-jpsi-near-threshold-photopr.name: GlueX near-threshold J/psi photoproduction

summary.plain: GlueX measured how often a photon striking a proton produces a J/ψ particle, from 11.8 GeV all the way down to the production threshold. It saw no sign of the LHCb pentaquark candidates in this channel and set upper limits.

result:gluex-jpsi-near-threshold-photopr.title: First measurement of near-threshold J/ψ exclusive photoproduction off the proton

result:grapes-3-thundercloud-potential-2.key_value_text: Thundercloud potential of 1.3 GV (storm of 1 December 2014)
result:grapes-3-thundercloud-potential-2.name: Electrical properties of a thundercloud from muon imaging

summary.plain: Thunderstorms change how many cosmic-ray muons reach the ground. GRAPES-3 used those changes to infer that one storm on 1 December 2014 built up an electric potential of 1.3 billion volts, estimating the cloud's height and size from field monitors.

result:grapes-3-thundercloud-potential-2.title: Measurement of the Electrical Properties of a Thundercloud Through Muon Imaging by the GRAPES-3 Experiment

result:hades-cc-dielectron-first-measure.name: HADES dielectron production in 12C+12C collisions at 2 AGeV

summary.plain: HADES's first physics result: the first measurement of the invariant-mass spectrum of electron-positron pairs from carbon-carbon collisions at 2 GeV per nucleon, over five orders of magnitude, showing an excess over pion and eta decays above 0.15 GeV/c^2.

result:hades-cc-dielectron-first-measure.title: Dielectron production in 12C+12C collisions at 2 AGeV with HADES

result:hades-dilepton-emission-baryon-ri.key_value_text: average temperature of the radiating fireball in Au+Au at sqrt(sNN) = 2.42 GeV: 71.8 ± 2.1 MeV
result:hades-dilepton-emission-baryon-ri.name: HADES first observation of dilepton emission from baryon-rich QCD matter

summary.plain: HADES recorded the electron-positron pairs radiated by the hot, dense fireball in gold-gold collisions, and reports the first observation of dilepton emission from QCD matter at high net-baryon density, like the matter in neutron-star mergers. The fireball temperature came out at about 72 MeV.

result:hades-dilepton-emission-baryon-ri.title: Probing dense baryon-rich matter with virtual photons

result:hades-flow-harmonics-au-au-2020.name: HADES flow harmonics of protons, deuterons and tritons in Au+Au at 2.4 GeV

summary.plain: HADES measured how protons, deuterons and tritons stream out of gold-gold collisions at 2.4 GeV, with flow coefficients up to the sixth order, giving a detailed picture of the pressure of the fireball and constraining the equation of state of dense baryonic matter.

result:hades-flow-harmonics-au-au-2020.title: Directed, elliptic and higher order flow harmonics of protons, deuterons and tritons in Au+Au collisions at sqrt(sNN) = 2.4 GeV

result:hagar-crab-detection-2019.key_value_text: Time-averaged flux (1.64 +- 0.09) x 10^-10 photons cm^-2 s^-1 above 230 GeV
result:hagar-crab-detection-2019.name: HAGAR detects the Crab Nebula at about 20 sigma with nine years of data

summary.plain: Nine years of HAGAR observations of the Crab Nebula, about 219 hours, show gamma rays above 230 GeV at a significance of about 20 sigma and track the long-term performance of the array.

result:hagar-crab-detection-2019.title: VHE Gamma-ray Observation of Crab Nebula with HAGAR Telescope Array

result:happex-i-ep-asymmetry-q2-0477-200.name: HAPPEX-I: parity-violating asymmetry in elastic electron-proton scattering at Q^2 = 0.477 (GeV/c)^2

summary.plain: A new HAPPEX measurement of the tiny difference in how spin-polarised electrons scatter from protons, made with an electron source and a Compton polarimeter that were firsts for such an experiment. It left room for only a small strange-quark contribution.

result:happex-i-ep-asymmetry-q2-0477-200.title: New Measurement of Parity Violation in Elastic Electron-Proton Scattering and Implications for Strange Form Factors

result:happex-ii-nucleon-strange-form-fa.name: HAPPEX-II and HAPPEX-He: strange form factors at Q^2 about 0.1 GeV^2

summary.plain: Measurements of how 3 GeV electrons scatter from hydrogen and helium at very small angles. They pin down the strange-quark contribution to the proton's charge and magnetism far more tightly than before, and it is consistent with zero.

result:happex-ii-nucleon-strange-form-fa.title: Precision Measurements of the Nucleon Strange Form Factors at Q^2 ~0.1 GeV^2

result:happex-iii-strange-vector-form-fa.name: HAPPEX-III: strange vector form factors of the proton at Q^2 = 0.624 GeV^2

summary.plain: HAPPEX-III repeated the measurement at a higher momentum transfer, where an earlier experiment had hinted at a strange-quark effect. It found none: the contribution is consistent with zero, and with all other data at most a few percent of the proton's form factors.

result:happex-iii-strange-vector-form-fa.title: New Precision Limit on the Strange Vector Form Factors of the Proton

result:hdms-final-setup-first-results-20.name: First Results from the HDMS experiment in the Final Setup

summary.plain: First data from the final HDMS set-up, with an enriched germanium-73 crystal at the centre: how well the detector worked and what background it saw.

result:hdms-final-setup-first-results-20.title: First Results from the HDMS experiment in the Final Setup

result:hdms-prototype-first-results-2000.name: First Results from the Heidelberg Dark Matter Search Experiment

summary.plain: After about 15 months in the Gran Sasso laboratory the HDMS prototype, two nested germanium crystals, gave its first limits on how strongly dark matter particles can interact with ordinary nuclei.

result:hdms-prototype-first-results-2000.title: First Results from the Heidelberg Dark Matter Search Experiment

result:hdms-spin-dependent-wimp-neutron-.key_value_text: Improves the best existing limits on the WIMP-neutron spin-dependent cross-section (previously from xenon-129) for low WIMP masses.
result:hdms-spin-dependent-wimp-neutron-.name: Limits on the spin-dependent WIMP-neutron cross section from HDMS (as reported in a 2006 Physica Scripta paper citing Phys. Lett. B 609, 226)

summary.plain: With its enriched germanium-73 crystal, HDMS gave a better limit than xenon-129 experiments on how strongly light dark matter particles could couple to neutrons.

result:hdms-spin-dependent-wimp-neutron-.title: Limits on the spin-dependent WIMP-neutron cross section from HDMS (as reported in a 2006 Physica Scripta paper citing Phys. Lett. B 609, 226)

result:hegra-cassiopeia-a-evidence-2001.key_value_text: Flux (5.8 +- 1.2 stat +- 1.2 syst) x 10^-9 ph m^-2 s^-1 above 1 TeV
result:hegra-cassiopeia-a-evidence-2001.name: HEGRA finds evidence for TeV gamma rays from Cassiopeia A

summary.plain: After 232 hours of observation, HEGRA's stereoscopic telescopes detected TeV gamma rays from the supernova remnant Cassiopeia A at the 5 sigma level, the first TeV source reported on the "centi-Crab" scale, about a hundredth of the Crab's brightness.

result:hegra-cassiopeia-a-evidence-2001.title: Evidence for TeV gamma ray emission from Cassiopeia A

result:hegra-crab-spectrum-2004.name: HEGRA measures the Crab Nebula spectrum from 500 GeV to 80 TeV

summary.plain: Nearly 400 hours of HEGRA data on the Crab Nebula give its gamma-ray spectrum from 500 GeV up to 80 TeV, well matched by inverse-Compton models, with an average magnetic field of about 160 microgauss in the nebula.

result:hegra-crab-spectrum-2004.title: The Crab Nebula and Pulsar between 500 GeV and 80 TeV: Observations with the HEGRA stereoscopic air Cherenkov telescopes

result:heidelberg-moscow-evidence-claim-.name: Evidence for Neutrinoless Double Beta Decay
result:heidelberg-moscow-evidence-claim-.significance: 97% (2.2 sigma) with the Bayesian method; 99.8% c.l. (3.1 sigma) with the method recommended by the Particle Data Group

summary.plain: Four members of the Heidelberg-Moscow team re-analysed the 1990-2000 data and reported evidence for neutrinoless double beta decay in germanium-76, at 2.2 to 3.1 sigma depending on the method. The claim was published by part of the collaboration only and was later tested by other germanium experiments.

result:heidelberg-moscow-evidence-claim-.title: Evidence for Neutrinoless Double Beta Decay

result:heidelberg-moscow-majorana-mass-l.key_value_text: T1/2(0vbb, 76Ge) > 5.7e25 yr (90 % C.L.); effective Majorana neutrino mass < 0.2 eV
result:heidelberg-moscow-majorana-mass-l.name: Limits on the Majorana neutrino mass in the 0.1 eV range

summary.plain: After 24 kg-years of data with pulse-shape selection, the Heidelberg-Moscow experiment saw no neutrinoless double beta decay in germanium-76. The half-life must exceed 5.7 x 10^25 years, which rules out an effective Majorana neutrino mass above 0.2 eV.

result:heidelberg-moscow-majorana-mass-l.title: Limits on the Majorana neutrino mass in the 0.1 eV range

result:helios-transverse-energy-o-nucleu.name: HELIOS transverse-energy distributions in oxygen-nucleus collisions

summary.plain: HELIOS measured how much transverse energy comes out of collisions of 60 and 200 GeV per nucleon oxygen nuclei with aluminium, silver and tungsten targets, over five orders of magnitude in cross-section, and used it to estimate the energy density reached.

result:helios-transverse-energy-o-nucleu.title: The transverse energy distribution in 16O-nucleus collisions at 60 and 200 GeV per nucleon

result:herab-bbbar-production-cross-sect.name: HERA-B b-bbar production cross section in 920 GeV proton-nucleus collisions

summary.plain: From a short commissioning-period run in 2000, HERA-B measured how often a 920 GeV proton striking carbon or titanium produces a pair of bottom quarks, tagging them through J/psi mesons decaying away from the target.

result:herab-bbbar-production-cross-sect.title: Measurement of the b-bbar production cross section in 920 GeV fixed-target proton-nucleus collisions

result:herab-jpsi-production-cross-secti.name: HERA-B J/psi production cross section in 920 GeV/c proton-nucleus interactions

summary.plain: HERA-B measured the production of J/psi mesons in 920 GeV proton collisions on carbon, titanium and tungsten targets, both at mid-rapidity and in total, using the data from its 2002-2003 run.

result:herab-jpsi-production-cross-secti.title: Measurement of the J/Psi production cross section in 920 GeV/c fixed-target proton-nucleus interactions

result:herald-first-demonstration-2023.name: First Demonstration of the HeRALD Superfluid Helium Detector Concept

summary.plain: A 10 g helium prototype showed for the first time that individual helium atoms knocked off the surface of the liquid can be detected, a signal the full detector needs. The prototype could already be sensitive to dark matter masses down to 220 MeV.

result:herald-first-demonstration-2023.title: First Demonstration of the HeRALD Superfluid Helium Detector Concept

result:herald-scintillation-yield-2021.name: Scintillation yield from electronic and nuclear recoils in superfluid $^4$He

summary.plain: A 16 cm^3 sample of superfluid helium viewed by six photomultiplier tubes was used to measure how much light electron and nuclear recoils produce, which sets how well a helium dark matter detector can tell signal from background.

result:herald-scintillation-yield-2021.title: Scintillation yield from electronic and nuclear recoils in superfluid $^4$He

result:herb-e288-upsilon-observation-197.name: Observation of a Dimuon Resonance at 9.5 GeV in 400-GeV Proton-Nucleus Collisions

summary.plain: The E288 team at Fermilab reported a clear bump in pairs of muons at 9.5 GeV from 400 GeV proton collisions. It was a new particle, the upsilon, later understood as a bottom quark bound to its antiquark.

result:herb-e288-upsilon-observation-197.title: Observation of a Dimuon Resonance at 9.5 GeV in 400-GeV Proton-Nucleus Collisions

result:hermes-g1-proton-deuteron-neutron.name: HERMES precise determination of the spin structure function g1 of the proton, deuteron and neutron

summary.plain: HERMES measured how the proton's and deuteron's spin is carried by quarks, with high precision over a wide range of momentum fraction, using polarised positrons on polarised hydrogen and deuterium gas, and derived the neutron's spin structure function.

result:hermes-g1-proton-deuteron-neutron.title: Precise determination of the spin structure function g1 of the proton, deuteron and neutron

result:hermes-quark-helicity-distributio.name: HERMES quark helicity distributions for up, down and strange quarks

summary.plain: Using spin asymmetries of identified pions and kaons, HERMES separated the contributions of up, down and strange quarks and antiquarks to the proton's spin, finding no significant strange-quark polarisation.

result:hermes-quark-helicity-distributio.title: Quark helicity distributions in the nucleon for up, down, and strange quarks from semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering

result:hires-gzk-suppression-2007.name: First observation of the GZK suppression

summary.plain: HiRes saw the flux of the most energetic cosmic rays drop sharply at about 6 × 10¹⁹ eV, where intergalactic radiation is expected to slow protons down. The collaboration quotes a significance of five standard deviations.

result:hires-gzk-suppression-2007.title: First Observation of the Greisen-Zatsepin-Kuzmin Suppression

result:holmes-neutrino-mass-limit-2025.name: Most stringent bound on electron neutrino mass obtained with a scalable low temperature microcalorimeter array

summary.plain: HOLMES watched holmium-163 decays in an array of ultra-cold detectors for two months and found no neutrino mass signal: the electron neutrino weighs less than 27 electron-volts at 90% credibility. The paper called it the most stringent bound from this calorimetric method; ECHo later reported a lower limit.

result:holmes-neutrino-mass-limit-2025.title: Most stringent bound on electron neutrino mass obtained with a scalable low temperature microcalorimeter array

result:homestake-flux-measurement-1998.name: Measurement of the Solar Electron Neutrino Flux with the Homestake Chlorine Detector

summary.plain: The Homestake chlorine detector had been measuring solar neutrinos since 1970; this paper reports the combined result of 108 extractions, a solar-neutrino-induced argon-37 production rate of 2.56 SNU. In his Nobel lecture Raymond Davis Jr. sets the measured 2.56 SNU against the standard solar model's 7.6 SNU, about a third of the predicted rate: the solar neutrino problem.

result:homestake-flux-measurement-1998.title: Measurement of the Solar Electron Neutrino Flux with the Homestake Chlorine Detector

result:hps-2016-engineering-run-prompt-a.name: HPS 2016 engineering run: prompt and displaced dark-photon searches

summary.plain: From its 2016 engineering run HPS reports both a prompt-resonance search (39-179 MeV) and its first search for dark photons that decay a short distance from the target; neither saw a signal, and the second lacked enough data to set limits.

result:hps-2016-engineering-run-prompt-a.title: Searching for Prompt and Long-Lived Dark Photons in Electro-Produced e+e- Pairs with the Heavy Photon Search Experiment at JLab

result:hps-first-search-2015-engineering.name: HPS first dark-photon search (2015 engineering run)

summary.plain: HPS's first data, taken in a 2015 engineering run, showed no sign of a dark photon with mass between 19 and 81 MeV, setting limits on its coupling to ordinary photons at the level of 6 x 10^-6 and showing the whole experiment worked.

result:hps-first-search-2015-engineering.title: Search for a Dark Photon in Electro-Produced e+e- Pairs with the Heavy Photon Search Experiment at JLab

result:hrs-qed-four-lepton-test-1990.key_value_text: 17 e+e-e+e-, 24 e+e-mu+mu- and 1 mu+mu-mu+mu- events with pair masses above 1 GeV/c^2 for 291 pb^-1
result:hrs-qed-four-lepton-test-1990.name: Test of QED to fourth order by study of four-lepton final states in e+e- interactions at 29 GeV with the HRS detector

summary.plain: The HRS experiment at PEP counted events with four charged leptons in electron-positron collisions at 29 GeV and compared them with the full fourth-order QED calculation, which agreed reasonably well with the data.

result:hrs-qed-four-lepton-test-1990.title: Test of QED to fourth order by study of four-lepton final states in e+e- interactions at 29 GeV with the HRS detector

result:icarus-hidden-sector-scalar-limit.key_value_text: No new physics signal observed in a search for long-lived particles from kaon decay that decay to two muons, with NuMI-beam data corresponding to 2.41×10²⁰ protons-on-target; the paper reports "world-leading limits on heavy QCD axions, as well as for the Higgs portal scalar among dedicated searches"
result:icarus-hidden-sector-scalar-limit.name: Search for a Hidden Sector Scalar from Kaon Decay in the Di-Muon Final State at ICARUS

summary.plain: ICARUS searched for a hidden-sector particle that could be produced in kaon decays and then decay into two muons inside the detector. It saw no signal and set limits; the paper describes them as world-leading for heavy QCD axions and, among dedicated searches, for the Higgs portal scalar.

result:icarus-hidden-sector-scalar-limit.title: Search for a Hidden Sector Scalar from Kaon Decay in the Di-Muon Final State at ICARUS

result:icecube-deepcore-atmospheric-osci.name: Atmospheric neutrino mixing measurement with IceCube DeepCore

summary.plain: IceCube's DeepCore sub-array measured how atmospheric neutrinos change type on their way through the Earth, using 2011–2019 data with improved calibration. The collaboration says the 40% error reduction makes this the most precise measurement of oscillation parameters using atmospheric neutrinos, and that the results are compatible and complementary to those from accelerator beams.

result:icecube-deepcore-atmospheric-osci.title: Measurement of Atmospheric Neutrino Mixing with Improved IceCube DeepCore Calibration and Data Processing

result:icecube-evidence-extraterrestrial.key_value_text: 28 events, purely atmospheric origin rejected at 4σ
result:icecube-evidence-extraterrestrial.name: Evidence for high-energy extraterrestrial neutrinos
result:icecube-evidence-extraterrestrial.significance: 4σ (purely atmospheric origin rejected, both searches combined)

summary.plain: IceCube reported 28 high-energy neutrino events that interact inside the detector. The collaboration says a purely atmospheric origin is rejected for these events at the 4σ level, and that their properties are consistent with generic predictions for an additional component of extraterrestrial origin.

result:icecube-evidence-extraterrestrial.title: Evidence for High-Energy Extraterrestrial Neutrinos at the IceCube Detector

result:icecube-galactic-plane-neutrinos-.name: Observation of high-energy neutrinos from the Galactic plane

summary.plain: Using machine learning on ten years of data, IceCube identified neutrino emission from the plane of our own Milky Way at the 4.5σ level of significance. The signal is consistent with modelled diffuse emission from the Galactic plane, but could also arise from a population of unresolved point sources.

result:icecube-galactic-plane-neutrinos-.title: Observation of high-energy neutrinos from the Galactic plane

result:icecube-glashow-resonance-candida.name: Detection of a particle shower at the Glashow resonance

summary.plain: IceCube detected a single particle shower with an energy of about 6 PeV (six thousand trillion electronvolts) that is consistent with being created at the Glashow resonance: the resonant formation of a W⁻ boson when a high-energy electron antineutrino meets an electron.

result:icecube-glashow-resonance-candida.title: Detection of a particle shower at the Glashow resonance with IceCube

result:icecube-ngc-1068-evidence-2022.name: Evidence for neutrino emission from NGC 1068

summary.plain: IceCube found an excess of about 79 neutrinos associated with the nearby active galaxy NGC 1068, at a significance of 4.2σ. The collaboration interprets it as direct evidence of TeV neutrino emission from a nearby active galaxy, and says the inferred neutrino flux exceeds the potential TeV gamma-ray flux by at least one order of magnitude.

result:icecube-ngc-1068-evidence-2022.title: Evidence for neutrino emission from the nearby active galaxy NGC 1068

result:icecube-sterile-neutrino-search-2.key_value_text: Best fit sin²(2θ₂₄) = 0.10, Δm²₄₁ = 4.5 eV²; consistent with no sterile neutrino, p = 8.0%
result:icecube-sterile-neutrino-search-2.name: eV-scale sterile neutrino search with eight years of atmospheric muon neutrinos

summary.plain: IceCube searched eight years of atmospheric muon-neutrino data for a fourth, 'sterile' kind of neutrino that would distort how atmospheric neutrinos pass through the Earth. The best-fit point is consistent with no sterile neutrino (p-value 8.0%).

result:icecube-sterile-neutrino-search-2.title: An eV-scale sterile neutrino search using eight years of atmospheric muon neutrino data from the IceCube Neutrino Observatory

result:icecube-txs-0506-056-multimesseng.name: Multimessenger observation of blazar TXS 0506+056 with IceCube-170922A

summary.plain: On 22 September 2017 IceCube detected a neutrino of about 290 TeV whose arrival direction was consistent with a known gamma-ray blazar, TXS 0506+056, that was observed to be in a flaring state. Telescopes from radio waves to gamma rays followed up, and the collaboration says the coincidence suggests that blazars may be a source of high-energy neutrinos.

result:icecube-txs-0506-056-multimesseng.title: Multi-messenger observations of a flaring blazar coincident with high-energy neutrino IceCube-170922A

result:icecube-txs-0506-056-prior-neutri.name: Evidence for a 2014–2015 neutrino flare from TXS 0506+056
result:icecube-txs-0506-056-prior-neutri.significance: 3.5σ (time-variable flux, excess from the direction of TXS 0506+056)

summary.plain: Searching 9.5 years of IceCube data after the 2017 alert, the collaboration found an excess of high-energy neutrino events at the position of the same blazar between September 2014 and March 2015, which it describes as 3.5σ evidence for neutrino emission from that direction, independent of and prior to the 2017 flare.

result:icecube-txs-0506-056-prior-neutri.title: Neutrino emission from the direction of the blazar TXS 0506+056 prior to the IceCube-170922A alert

result:igex-dm-improved-constraints-2001.name: Improved constraints on WIMPs from the International Germanium Experiment IGEX

result:mainz-final-neutrino-mass-limit-2.title: Final Results from phase II of the Mainz Neutrino Mass Search in Tritium β Decay

result:mark-i-psi-discovery-1974.title: Discovery of a Narrow Resonance in e+e− Annihilation

result:mark-j-three-jet-discovery-1979.title: Discovery of Three-Jet Events and a Test of Quantum Chromodynamics at PETRA

result:meg-ii-mu-to-e-gamma-limit-2024.title: A search for mu+ -> e+ gamma with the first dataset of the MEG II experiment

result:meg-mu-to-e-gamma-limit-2016.title: Search for the Lepton Flavour Violating Decay mu+ -> e+ gamma with the Full Dataset of the MEG Experiment

result:microboone-no-low-energy-excess-2.key_value_text: Three independent electron-neutrino searches (exclusive 1-proton, semi-inclusive pion-less, fully inclusive) all consistent with nominal νe rate expectations from the BNB; no excess of electron neutrino events observed in any of the three

result:microboone-no-low-energy-excess-2.title: Search for an Excess of Electron Neutrino Interactions in MicroBooNE Using Multiple Final State Topologies

result:milagro-10tev-excess-2008.name: Milagro finds two localized regions of excess 10-TeV cosmic rays

result:milagro-cygnus-region-2006.name: Milagro discovers TeV gamma-ray emission from the Cygnus region

result:milagro-cygnus-region-2006.title: Discovery of TeV Gamma-Ray Emission from the Cygnus Region of the Galaxy

result:mimac-electron-recoil-discriminat.name: MIMAC low energy electron-recoil discrimination measured with fast neutrons

result:mimac-electron-recoil-discriminat.title: MIMAC low energy electron-recoil discrimination measured with fast neutrons

result:mimac-first-directional-limits-20.name: First Directional Dark Matter Limits from the MIMAC μ-TPC Detector

result:mimac-first-directional-limits-20.title: First Directional Dark Matter Limits from the MIMAC μ-TPC Detector

result:mimac-kev-proton-carbon-direction.name: Directional detection of keV proton and carbon recoils with MIMAC

result:mimac-kev-proton-carbon-direction.title: Directional detection of keV proton and carbon recoils with MIMAC

result:mimac-radon-progeny-tracks-2015.name: First detection of tracks of radon progeny recoils by MIMAC

summary.plain: In the Modane underground laboratory MIMAC recorded, for the first time, the energy and three-dimensional tracks of low-energy nuclear recoils from radon decay products, showing the detector can see recoil directions.

result:mimac-radon-progeny-tracks-2015.title: First detection of tracks of radon progeny recoils by MIMAC

result:minerva-axial-form-factor-2023.key_value_text: Nucleon axial charge radius rA = 0.73 ± 0.17 fm, extracted from what the authors describe as, to their knowledge, the first high-statistics ν̄μp→μ⁺n cross-section measurement on free (hydrogen) protons
result:minerva-axial-form-factor-2023.name: Measurement of the axial vector form factor from antineutrino–proton scattering

result:minerva-axial-form-factor-2023.title: Measurement of the axial vector form factor from antineutrino–proton scattering

result:miniboone-low-energy-excess-2021.title: Updated MiniBooNE Neutrino Oscillation Results with Increased Data and New Background Studies

result:minos-oscillation-measurement-201.name: Measurement of Neutrino and Antineutrino Oscillations Using Beam and Atmospheric Data in MINOS

result:minos-oscillation-measurement-201.title: Measurement of Neutrino and Antineutrino Oscillations Using Beam and Atmospheric Data in MINOS

result:minos-sterile-neutrino-limit-2016.name: Search for Sterile Neutrinos Mixing with Muon Neutrinos in MINOS

result:minos-sterile-neutrino-limit-2016.title: Search for Sterile Neutrinos Mixing with Muon Neutrinos in MINOS

result:moscab-fast-neutron-detection-202.name: Effective exploitation of a geyser bubble-chamber equipment as a background-free fast neutron detector

result:moscab-fast-neutron-detection-202.title: Effective exploitation of a geyser bubble-chamber equipment as a background-free fast neutron detector

result:moscab-geyser-chamber-tests-2017.name: MOSCAB: A geyser-concept bubble chamber to be used in a dark matter search

result:moscab-geyser-chamber-tests-2017.title: MOSCAB: A geyser-concept bubble chamber to be used in a dark matter search

result:mulan-detailed-report-2012.name: Detailed Report of the MuLan Measurement of the Positive Muon Lifetime and Determination of the Fermi Constant
result:mulan-detailed-report-2012.significance: Lifetime 1.0 ppm; Fermi constant to 0.5 ppm

result:mulan-detailed-report-2012.title: Detailed Report of the MuLan Measurement of the Positive Muon Lifetime and Determination of the Fermi Constant

result:mulan-fermi-constant-2010.name: Measurement of the Positive Muon Lifetime and Determination of the Fermi Constant to Part-per-Million Precision

summary.plain: MuLan timed more than two trillion muon decays and measured the muon lifetime to one part in a million, the most precise lifetime ever measured for a particle. From it the strength of the weak force, the Fermi constant, follows to 0.6 parts per million.

result:mulan-fermi-constant-2010.title: Measurement of the Positive Muon Lifetime and Determination of the Fermi Constant to Part-per-Million Precision

result:muon-g-2-measurement-2021.name: Measurement of the Positive Muon Anomalous Magnetic Moment to 0.46 ppm

result:muon-g-2-measurement-2021.title: Measurement of the Positive Muon Anomalous Magnetic Moment to 0.46 ppm

result:muon-g-2-measurement-2023.name: Measurement of the Positive Muon Anomalous Magnetic Moment to 0.20 ppm

result:muon-g-2-measurement-2023.title: Measurement of the Positive Muon Anomalous Magnetic Moment to 0.20 ppm

result:muon-g-2-measurement-2025.title: Measurement of the Positive Muon Anomalous Magnetic Moment to 127 ppb

result:na35-strangeness-enhancement-s-s-.name: NA35 enhanced strange-particle production in central sulphur-sulphur collisions

result:na35-strangeness-enhancement-s-s-.title: Neutral strange particle production in sulphur-sulphur and proton-sulphur collisions at 200 GeV/nucleon

result:na38-jpsi-transverse-energy-depen.name: NA38 J/psi yield versus transverse energy in oxygen-uranium collisions

result:na38-jpsi-transverse-energy-depen.title: The production of J/psi in 200 GeV/nucleon oxygen-uranium interactions

result:na44-particle-production-central-.name: NA44 particle production and freeze-out in central Pb+Pb collisions

result:na44-particle-production-central-.title: Particle production in central Pb+Pb collisions at 158 A GeV/c

result:na49-pion-kaon-energy-dependence-.name: NA49 energy dependence of pion and kaon production in central Pb+Pb collisions

result:na49-pion-kaon-energy-dependence-.title: Energy Dependence of Pion and Kaon Production in Central Pb+Pb Collisions

result:na49-pion-kaon-onset-of-deconfine.title: Pion and kaon production in central Pb+Pb collisions at 20A and 30A GeV: Evidence for the onset of deconfinement

result:na50-anomalous-jpsi-suppression-p.title: Anomalous J/ψ suppression in Pb-Pb interactions at 158 GeV/c per nucleon

result:na57-central-to-peripheral-nuclea.title: Central-to-peripheral nuclear modification factors in Pb-Pb collisions at sqrt(s_NN) = 17.3 GeV

result:na60-jpsi-in-in-suppression-2007.name: NA60 J/psi production in indium-indium collisions

result:na60-jpsi-in-in-suppression-2007.title: J/psi production in Indium-Indium collisions at 158 GeV/nucleon

result:na60-rho-spectral-function-in-in-.name: NA60 first measurement of the rho spectral function in high-energy nuclear collisions

result:na60-rho-spectral-function-in-in-.title: First Measurement of the rho Spectral Function in High-Energy Nuclear Collisions

result:na61-shine-bebe-pion-production-e.name: NA61/SHINE pi- production in 7Be+9Be at 19A to 150A GeV/c

result:na61-shine-pc-31gev-cross-section.name: NA61/SHINE p+C cross sections and pion spectra at 31 GeV/c (T2K replica target)

result:newage-0-3b-double-prime-2021.title: Direction-sensitive dark matter search with a low-background gaseous detector NEWAGE-0.3b''

result:newage-0-3b-prime-3d-vector-2020.name: First limits from a 3d-vector directional dark matter search with the NEWAGE-0.3b' detector

result:newage-0-3b-prime-3d-vector-2020.title: First limits from a 3d-vector directional dark matter search with the NEWAGE-0.3b' detector

result:newage-3d-vector-2023.name: Direction-sensitive dark matter search with three-dimensional vector-type tracking in NEWAGE

result:newage-3d-vector-2023.title: Direction-sensitive dark matter search with three-dimensional vector-type tracking in NEWAGE

result:newage-surface-laboratory-limit-2.name: Direction-sensitive dark matter search results in a surface laboratory

result:newage-surface-laboratory-limit-2.title: Direction-sensitive dark matter search results in a surface laboratory

result:newsdm-environmental-neutron-gran.name: Environmental sub-MeV neutron measurement at the Gran Sasso surface laboratory with a super-fine-grained nuclear emulsion detector

result:newsdm-first-directional-emulsion.title: First direction sensitive search for dark matter with a nuclear emulsion detector at a surface site

result:nist-bl1-neutron-lifetime-2013.name: Improved Determination of the Neutron Lifetime

summary.plain: The NIST beam experiment re-measured how well its neutron counter works, five times more precisely than before, and so updated its 2005 neutron lifetime to 887.7 seconds with an uncertainty of about 2.2 seconds.

result:nist-bl1-neutron-lifetime-2013.title: Improved Determination of the Neutron Lifetime

result:nist-bl2-molecular-hydrogen-2025.key_value_text: Charge exchange of trapped protons on molecular hydrogen demonstrated; BL1 lifetime unlikely to be significantly affected

result:nist-bl2-molecular-hydrogen-2025.title: Detection of molecular hydrogen in a neutron beam lifetime experiment

result:nomad-final-oscillation-limits-20.title: Final NOMAD results on nu_mu->nu_tau and nu_e->nu_tau oscillations including a new search for nu_tau appearance using hadronic tau decays

result:nova-t2k-joint-oscillation-analys.title: Joint neutrino oscillation analysis from the T2K and NOvA experiments

result:nusex-atmospheric-neutrino-flux-1.name: Experimental Study of Atmospheric Neutrino Flux in the NUSEX Experiment

result:nusex-atmospheric-neutrino-flux-1.title: Experimental Study of Atmospheric Neutrino Flux in the NUSEX Experiment

result:nusex-nucleon-decay-candidate-198.name: Mount Blanc experiment on nucleon stability

By 1985 it listed three nucleon-decay candidates among 31 contained events. No experiment has confirmed proton decay.

result:nusex-nucleon-decay-candidate-198.title: Mount Blanc experiment on nucleon stability

result:nutev-weak-mixing-angle-2002.name: A Precise Determination of Electroweak Parameters in Neutrino-Nucleon Scattering
result:nutev-weak-mixing-angle-2002.significance: three standard deviations above the standard model prediction

result:nutev-weak-mixing-angle-2002.title: A Precise Determination of Electroweak Parameters in Neutrino-Nucleon Scattering

result:opera-tau-neutrino-appearance-dis.name: Discovery of tau neutrino appearance in the CNGS neutrino beam with the OPERA experiment

result:opera-tau-neutrino-appearance-dis.title: Discovery of tau neutrino appearance in the CNGS neutrino beam with the OPERA experiment

result:orpheus-first-results-2004.title: First results with the ORPHEUS dark matter detector

result:orpheus-ssg-nuclear-recoil-respon.name: Detection of nuclear recoils in prototype dark matter detectors, made from Al, Sn and Zn Superheated Superconducting Granules

result:orpheus-ssg-nuclear-recoil-respon.title: Detection of nuclear recoils in prototype dark matter detectors, made from Al, Sn and Zn Superheated Superconducting Granules

result:oscura-single-electron-traps-2024.name: Studying single-electron traps in newly fabricated Skipper-CCDs for the Oscura experiment using the pocket-pumping technique

summary.plain: Oscura's first batches of sensors were studied for tiny defects that can fake a one-electron signal. One sensor, measured about 100 m underground, showed a single-electron rate of about two thousandths per pixel per day.

result:oscura-single-electron-traps-2024.title: Studying single-electron traps in newly fabricated Skipper-CCDs for the Oscura experiment using the pocket-pumping technique

result:oscura-skipper-ccd-sensors-2023.name: Skipper-CCD Sensors for the Oscura Experiment: Requirements and Preliminary Tests

result:oscura-skipper-ccd-sensors-2023.title: Skipper-CCD Sensors for the Oscura Experiment: Requirements and Preliminary Tests

result:palo-verde-initial-results-2000.title: Search for Neutrino Oscillations at the Palo Verde Nuclear Reactors

result:pandax-i-first-results-2014.name: First dark matter search results from the PandaX-I experiment

result:pandax-i-low-mass-full-exposure-2.title: Low-mass dark matter search results from full exposure of PandaX-I experiment

result:pandax-ii-54-ton-day-2017.name: Dark Matter Results From 54-Ton-Day Exposure of PandaX-II Experiment

result:pandax-ii-54-ton-day-2017.title: Dark Matter Results From 54-Ton-Day Exposure of PandaX-II Experiment

result:pandax-ii-98-7-day-2016.name: Dark Matter Results from First 98.7-day Data of PandaX-II Experiment

result:pandax-ii-full-exposure-2020.name: Results of Dark Matter Search using the Full PandaX-II Exposure
